cases.title: Contention Wall
cases.description: Rust drives 100 OS threads through one shared AtomicI64. Kain currently has no user-level OS-thread fanout in LLVM, so this is the zero-lock collapse proxy over the same total increment count.
cases.fairness_note: Do not read this as a completed concurrency win. It is the benchmark shape Kain must graduate toward once collapse can be shared safely across spawned workers.

language_notes.javascript: Dependency-free Node uses a scalar proxy here so worker startup and SharedArrayBuffer scheduling do not dominate the case.
language_notes.python: Dependency-free CPython uses a scalar proxy here because locked threads would mostly measure GIL and lock scheduling overhead.

cases.title: Ghost Mirror
cases.description: Rust mirrors a 1 MiB payload through a std TCP loopback channel. Kain mirrors authority state with entangle and mutates a 1 MiB helper-owned buffer in-process.
cases.fairness_note: Kain entangle is currently in-process world mirroring, not a two-process transport. This case measures serialization/transport tax versus compiler-owned mirror semantics.

cases.title: Evolutionary Loop
cases.description: Rust uses runtime feature detection to choose a math lane. Kain expresses the same decision as converge/orchestrate lanes.
cases.fairness_note: Current Kain converge records and selects lanes; it does not yet race AVX-512 kernels or autotune silicon. This benchmark is the durable harness slot for that future backend.

cases.title: Scoped Ownership Memory Cell
cases.description: A smaller first-class ownership smoke benchmark: Kain uses collapse/observe/decay over a helper-owned heap cell; Rust uses an owned Box mutation and drop.
cases.fairness_note: This is a direct memory-lifecycle smoke, not a contention test.

cases.title: Branch Dispatch
cases.description: Integer match/branch dispatch with mixed arithmetic. This catches control-flow lowering, branch prediction, and basic optimizer quality.
cases.fairness_note: Both sides use deterministic scalar control flow and no external dependencies.

cases.title: Call Chain
cases.description: Deep small-function call graph inside a hot loop. This measures call overhead, inlining assumptions, and arithmetic lowering.
cases.fairness_note: Rust functions are marked inline(never) to keep this from becoming a pure optimizer-elimination benchmark.

cases.title: Memory Stream
cases.description: Sequential write/read over a helper-owned integer buffer. Kain uses raw memory helpers under collapse/observe; Rust uses a Vec<i64>.
cases.fairness_note: This is a direct memory-throughput smoke, not a SIMD memcpy benchmark.

cases.title: Allocation Churn
cases.description: Many small allocate/write/read/free cycles. Kain uses alloc_zeroed plus decay; Rust uses Box allocation and drop.
cases.fairness_note: This is intentionally allocator-heavy and will expose runtime bookkeeping overhead.

cases.title: Scalar Mix
cases.description: Hot scalar loop with top-level const expressions and a checksum guard. This case exercises LLVM top-level const resolution directly in the benchmark lane.
cases.fairness_note: Both sides use local top-level consts plus a deterministic checksum gate; this is the benchmarked path for the repaired const lowering.

cases.title: Recursive Sum
cases.description: Recursive integer aggregation in a hot loop. This catches call-stack lowering, recursion overhead, and tail-call assumptions without external dependencies.
cases.fairness_note: Both sides use the same pure recursive helper and identical loop counts; no runtime libraries beyond std builtins are involved.

cases.title: String Ops
cases.description: Repeated substring search and string length/indexing over top-level string consts. This probes text lowering and branchy search loops without external dependencies.
cases.fairness_note: Both sides stay on ASCII-only text and pure std/string builtins so search semantics remain directly comparable.

cases.title: Array Scan
cases.description: Nested array indexing and weighted accumulation over a fixed integer list. This stresses bounds handling, indexing, and simple loop lowering.
cases.fairness_note: Both sides use fixed local arrays and the same loop counts; there are no imported containers or external dependencies.

cases.title: Struct Method Dispatch
cases.description: Construct small records and call an instance method in a hot loop. This catches aggregate layout and method-call lowering.
cases.fairness_note: Both sides allocate records on the stack/logical value path rather than external heaps.

cases.title: Option/Result Tagged Values
cases.description: Hot loop over Option and Result creation, branching, and unwrap paths. This probes tagged runtime value overhead.
cases.fairness_note: Rust uses std Option/Result; Kain uses its native tagged runtime path.
